candidates.claim: On the eight-B200 DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash node, trial a capped asynchronous draft cache that prepares likely verification continuations while the target verifies the current MTP batch. A scheduler would spend a per-request token and memory budget only when traces show material draft wait and verification outcomes that can be predicted affordably; otherwise it would use fixed MTP. Prepared continuations would carry request and KV-state epochs and expire on mismatch, preemption, prefix-cache reset, or budget pressure. This could reduce TPOT when a prepared continuation matches, but discarded work could reduce throughput. No supplied source measures draft wait, outcome predictability, or discarded-work cost for this model. Reported SSD gains elsewhere are author claims. Compare within the same eight-GPU budget against qualified fixed MTP and a static branch policy.

alternatives: Fixed MTP already hides most drafting time.
Any apparent gain comes from asynchronous DP coordination or configuration drift.
